selected_primary_idea.title: ProxyGate: Evidence-Gated Readiness Assessment for De-Extinction Proxies
selected_primary_idea.summary: A design-only, uncertainty-aware decision architecture that requires genomic, phenotype, welfare, ecological, and governance gates before a proxy proposal can be conditionally reviewed.
selected_primary_idea.mechanism: Non-compensatory gates prevent strong evidence in one domain from hiding critical failure in another; robust scoring operates only among candidates that clear each gate.
falsification_conditions: Failure to reject a deep-time negative control such as a non-avian dinosaur.
Conditional reviewability despite unresolved welfare or governance failures.
Ecological benefit reversal relative to conventional conservation alternatives.
Decision dominated by assumptions rather than evidence.

rejected_ideas.reason: Exact historical-species restoration cannot be inferred from partial genomic and developmental evidence.
Any route that requires operational genetic, reproductive, or release procedures violates the research-design scope.
